title: West Punjab Special Tribunal Abolition Act 1948

sections.shortTitle: West Punjab Special Tribunal Abolition Act 1948
sections.description:
Short title and commencement

Act No
Act No. XVIII of 1948
West Punjab Special
Tribunal (Abolition) Act, 1948.
An Act to abolish the West Punjab Special Tribunal as constituted under
the Indian Independence (Special Tribunal) Order, 1947.
Whereas it is no longer necessary, having regard to
the volume and nature of the work before the West Punjab Tribunal, to continue
it
It is hereby enacted as follows:
1. Short title
and commencement.-(1) This
Act may be called the West Punjab Special Tribunal (Abolition) Act, 1948.
(2) It shall come into force at once.

sections.shortTitle: West Punjab Special Tribunal Abolition Act 1948
sections.description:
Powers of the Magistrate

Act No
Act No. XVIII of 1948
West Punjab Special
Tribunal (Abolition) Act, 1948.
An Act to abolish the West Punjab Special Tribunal as constituted under
the Indian Independence (Special Tribunal) Order, 1947.
Whereas it is no longer necessary, having regard to
the volume and nature of the work before the West Punjab Tribunal, to continue
it
It is hereby enacted as follows:
4. Powers of the
Magistrate,--The District Magistrate of Lahore, or any other
Magistrate subordinate to him to whom any of the cases may be transferred by
shall have all the powers vested in a
Special Tribunal under section 6 of the Criminal Law Amendment Ordinance, 1943.

sections.shortTitle: West Punjab Special Tribunal Abolition Act 1948
sections.description:
Procedure

Act No
Act No. XVIII of 1948
West Punjab Special
Tribunal (Abolition) Act, 1948.
An Act to abolish the West Punjab Special Tribunal as constituted under
the Indian Independence (Special Tribunal) Order, 1947.
Whereas it is no longer necessary, having regard to
the volume and nature of the work before the West Punjab Tribunal, to continue
it
It is hereby enacted as follows:
5. Procedure.---The District Magistrate
of Lahore, or the Magistrate to whom any of the cases is transferred by him,
shall proceed with the hearing of the cases from the stage each of the cases
has reached and he shall not be bound to recall or rehear any
witness. The evidence recorded and all the proceedings held before the Special
Tribunal shall be treated as if they had been recorded or held in the Court of
the District Magistrate of Lahore or the Magistrate to whom the case is
transferred by him, as the case may be.
